* WHERE...North facing reefs of Yap.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM ChST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized
beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Long-period swell, originating from distant
Typhoon Dolphin, is still expected to bring hazardous surf along
north-facing reefs through much of the weekend. As swells
diminish, surf is expected to subside below hazardous levels of 9
feet by Sunday night.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...West winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and seas
8 to 11 feet.

* WHERE...Marianas Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Until 5 AM ChST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Moderate to strong westerlies prevail
across the Marianas over the weekend as another resurgence in
the monsoon builds, likely to maintain moderate to strong winds
through the middle of next week. Combined seas of 8 to 11 feet
are expected over the next few days, remaining hazardous to
small craft through at least early next week.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Rota...

* WHEN...Until 700 PM ChST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 502 PM ChST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
training showers and thunderstorms. This is expected to cause
urban and small stream flooding.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1.6 to 2.4 inches are expected
over the area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Sinapalo, Songsong, Annex F, Tenetu, I Chenchon, Liyu, Ginalangan
(Chudan), Taimama, Tatgua, Matpo, Gampapa, As Niebes (Nieves),
Talo, Makmak, Agatasi (Payapai), Lempanai, Gayaugan (Kaan),
Gagani, Mananana and Finata.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
